notes:
I wasn't able to write any notes on Proverbs 12, because I couldn't read any of the sources.

I tried to open four pages at once: the Enduring Word commentary, Precept Austin's commentary, the NET Bible notes, and Wesley's notes on StudyLight. That first attempt failed because of a mistake in my code. Before I could fix it, I hit the limit on how many research steps I can take in one reply. As a result I have no page content for any of the 28 verses.

Your rules say to report only what the pages say and to leave out anything I couldn't find. Since I found nothing, I've left the notes out entirely rather than writing them from memory.

**If you ask me to try again,** I plan to read:
- **Verse-by-verse commentaries:** Enduring Word's Proverbs 12 page, Bible Hub's per-verse pages (which collect Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary, Matthew Henry and others), and Precept Austin's Proverbs 12 page.
- **Modern scholarship:** NET Bible notes, especially where the Hebrew is hard to translate. Verses 12, 26 and 27 are well known for this.
- **Different Protestant traditions:** Wesley's notes on StudyLight, plus searches of Ligonier, Desiring God, Grace to You and Got Questions for single verses. Likely ones are v. 4 (the noble wife), v. 10 (care for animals), v. 18 (words that wound or heal) and v. 25 (anxiety).
- **Catholic and Orthodox readings:** New Advent (Church Fathers) and Catholic.com.
- **Popular modern teaching:** searches on prosperity or word-of-faith use of v. 14 ("filled with good things"), v. 21 ("no harm befalls the righteous") and v. 24 (the diligent will rule).
